mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within the last month signals economic weakness, leading to negative investor sentiment and reduced S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over the past 3 months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS declines over the past 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month signals strengthening supply-side activity, which boosts investor confidence and increases S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the past month, it signals a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200k.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the past 3 months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST decreases by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate slows to less than 2% annually, it signals a restrictive monetary policy combined with economic deceleration, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3% and GDPC1 growth < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 2% in the past 3 months, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points, signals robust economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2% and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.
